mbm-1826.clue: I keep the radio a little off station.
mbm-1826.quote: My favorite patch of sun is beside a fence full of cicadas. If I tune just past the station, the soft hiss and the cicadas sound exactly like surf. My yard's a long way from the sea.

mbm-1827.clue: I paint the empty perches first.
mbm-1827.quote: I drew three fence posts in my bird book before the swallows arrived. Two birds landed on the left post and nobody chose the right. That empty post makes the page feel like the whole morning.

mbm-1828.clue: My grandmother calls the villain the coat rack.
mbm-1828.quote: We play a co-op adventure on her old television. The big boss has so many antlers she thought you could hang things on him. I laughed and missed the jump. She beat him while I was catching my breath.

mbm-1829.clue: My mittens have a snowflake scorecard.
mbm-1829.quote: On our ski trips my sister sketches the morning's first snow crystal on a card tucked into my cuff. At lunch we spread them beside the soup bowls and choose our favorite storm.

mbm-1830.clue: I keep the first and last chapters in different hands.
mbm-1830.quote: I rebuilt the worn cover of my oldest book with purple cloth from Mum's dress and green cloth from Dad's shirt. Close it and the two pieces meet down the middle, just like their Sunday walk.

mbm-1831.clue: The round postcard came by ordinary post.
mbm-1831.quote: A radio friend always described the view through his attic porthole. He finally sent me a round card painted with his rooftops. I pinned it above my set and called to tell him his window had arrived.

mbm-1832.clue: My butter dish has a rain gutter.
mbm-1832.quote: I built a clay roof over the butter and pinched one corner up for a little drainpipe. My sister poured honey over it to test the engineering. We ate the results off toast.

mbm-1833.clue: I quilt the stairs in pairs.
mbm-1833.quote: I made a blanket of houses with two steps to each front door. My father asked why they all had the same steps. Those two scraps came from the work shirt he wore building ours.

mbm-1834.clue: Even an empty tin should sound nice.
mbm-1834.quote: I dropped a bean in the camping coffee tin so I could find it by ear in the dark. My tent mate shook up three tins for breakfast. We found the coffee and invented a respectable little band.

mbm-1835.clue: I aimed for the shadow of the blue hat.
mbm-1835.quote: Grandpa wore his enormous blue sun hat on the practice green. He sat beside the cup so I could see the spot from the far end. I finally put one straight into his shadow.

mbm-1836.clue: Our disc came home by a different route.
mbm-1836.quote: At the park a little gust carried my throw over a hedge. It came back through a gap at knee height. The gardener on the other side had a straighter throw than either of us.

mbm-1837.clue: No two tentacles should be the same length.
mbm-1837.quote: I crocheted my niece a purple octopus while watching an extra-inning game. The last tentacle grew and grew. She uses the long one to tuck him in at night.

mbm-1838.clue: The mirror only gets half the picture.
mbm-1838.quote: My sister and I work out on opposite ends of a small gym. At the end of a set I look for her in the narrow mirror. I raise one thumb, and she sends one back.

mbm-1839.clue: My needle went round the cherry twice.
mbm-1839.quote: I quilted my aunt's cherry pie recipe into colored squares. The reddest cherry lifts like a flap and the cooking time is stitched underneath. She checks it even when the oven is empty.

mbm-1840.clue: I left a space by the jukebox.
mbm-1840.quote: My first ballroom teacher tapped the rhythm on the side of a jukebox with her ring. We took her dancing on her birthday. I could hear that little metallic click before I saw her hand.

mbm-1841.clue: I made a bowl for left-handed soup.
mbm-1841.quote: I shaped a pouring lip on the side my grandmother reaches for first. When we glazed it she asked for bright green so nobody else would mistake it for theirs. That lip fits her thumb exactly.

mbm-1842.clue: I always finish the ladder first.
mbm-1842.quote: My little cousin won't accept a model until somebody can climb into it. I make a tiny boarding ladder before I even paint the cockpit. He inspects it with one very solemn finger.

mbm-1843.clue: Run with me till the shutters change color.
mbm-1843.quote: The florist along my route opens her yellow shutters as I pass. When I get there early the street is slate blue. One morning I stopped to watch the whole block turn gold.

mbm-1844.clue: The quietest exhibit has a little squeak.
mbm-1844.quote: My favorite case holds an old wooden spinning top. I drew it six times. The guard opened a drawer and showed me the museum shop's replica, still spinning from his break.

mbm-1845.clue: I save one note for the doorway.
mbm-1845.quote: The marimba at my cousin's house has a low note that carries right down the hall. When supper's ready I hear a spoon against a plate and answer with that note. We always agree on the timing.

mbm-1846.clue: I shade my eyes to read the time in the water.
mbm-1846.quote: The bridge clock reflects in the canal. From my kayak the numbers are backward, but I know the long hand points at the bakery when the rolls are coming out.

mbm-1847.clue: I asked the DJ for a minute of quiet.
mbm-1847.quote: A friend was leaving town after the last song. We wanted to give him a proper cheer, so the DJ lowered the fader with the record still spinning. He heard every voice and danced to the cheer.

mbm-1848.clue: My uncle knows when I'm learning a new chord.
mbm-1848.quote: I rest the cuatro against the wall when I stop for tea. My uncle says the old boards carry every note into his kitchen. He taps twice on the wall when I finally get it clean.

mbm-1849.clue: We give the dog the first short throw.
mbm-1849.quote: Our dog brings back the frisbee only from shade. On a hot day we threw a whole zigzag beneath the trees and reached the far end of the park without taking a step in the sun.

mbm-1850.clue: Hold the striped spoon very still.
mbm-1850.quote: I make a marble vanish from a coffee spoon and appear under an eggcup. Grandpa painted the handle with stripes so the back row could follow. They watch the stripes and miss his wink.
